notes: Mustang Mach-E (EPA 2021-2026 rows with no displacement) is a separate electric model and is excluded.

NHRA ratings from 2009 on are NHRA-factored (e.g. GT 412-460 hp shown as 380-390 hp); modern matches are by displacement only and are noted per entry. NHRA has no sheets for 2002, 2004, 2018, 2020 or 2024-2026.

Ford brochures 1994-2004 are Ford Heritage Vault PDFs (text layer read directly; the 2002 one is Ford of Canada, in French). Ford releases 2012-2024 are archived media.ford.com pages (web.archive.org); 2005-2013 releases are cited through netcarshow reprints of Ford text. media.ford.com now redirects to fromtheroad.ford.com (403).
Kelley Blue Book trim-data errors: 1994 Cobra at 215, 1999 Cobra 316, 2001 Bullitt 260, 2004 Mach 1 310, GT500KR 500, 2016 GT350 blank, 2022 Mach 1 450 in the trim table (470 in the text).
MustangSpecs errors: 1996-97 V6 145, 1999-2002 V6 193, a 2002 SVT Cobra (none was built), 2011 "Shelby GT-350 500hp" (a Shelby American post-title conversion), 2013 GT500 650.

Dealer/tuner conversions are not listed as factory engines: Saleen, Roush, Steeda; Shelby American post-title cars (2011+ GT350, Super Snake, 2020-22 GT500 SE/KR/Code Red); dealer-installed Ford Racing Power Upgrade Packs. Shelby GT/GT-H (2006-08) are recorded as dealer_conversion.
Cobra Jet: Ford timeline says 50 CJs in 2008 and 250 more 2009-16, plus 50 in 2016 and 68 in 2018; all are no-VIN race cars. Only CJ years with a clear NHRA row and a second source are listed.
rpo field holds a short engine description; Ford engine (VIN) codes were not stated in the sources used and are omitted.
